effect: Central-bank independence, once lost, comes back over years. The credibility score the anchor follows each day (RqA, since build 26403824 an absolute target between 0.05 and 1) is multiplied by 0.55 while the government controls the central bank (cbAuto false) and by 1 otherwise, so restoring independence (pcQ) put the target back at once; and because the daily step only sees the state at tick time, taking control to set a rate and restoring independence on the same day cost nothing at all while the set rate decays only slowly toward the bank's rule. Now the factor returns from 0.55 to 1 in a straight line over 3 years (1,095 days) after the last day of government control, counted from the last daily step that saw control or from the day independence was restored, whichever is later; under control it stays 0.55 as before, and the anchor still follows its target at the game's own speeds (falls at 0.9, rises at 0.3 a year of the gap). (Up to build 26391432 the target was measured against a day-0 score, _orth0, and this patch also kept control out of that baseline; the game has since made the target absolute, so control before the first step costs in the original too.) Real independence is judged on its track record: a government that has overridden its central bank is priced as if it may do so again until years of non-interference have passed. Effect, with the other credibility terms held fixed (function test, anchor relative to the original's never-controlled anchor): a same-day take-and-restore now costs about as much credibility as a year of control (the anchor bottoms at 78% about 1.5 years later, 93% after 6 years; the original: no cost), toggling every month ends where permanent control does (56% vs 56% after 6 years), and a year of control followed by restoration recovers more slowly (71% instead of 86% 2 years after restoring). End to end (tests/m4.headless.mjs, China, seed 12345): a same-day take-and-restore on day 1 leaves the anchor at 94.0% of its starting value on day 61 and 91.4% on day 91, against 99.9% without this patch (measured on build 26403824). No restore cooldown is needed: restoring early never beats staying independent. Countries using an adopted strong currency (dollarized) keep factor 1 as in the original. State: country.geobalCbControlDay, written by the daily step while under control and by the restore action; absent means never controlled since the mod was loaded (factor 1, the original). Day 0 unchanged: every country starts with cbAuto true (measured at boot, the 16 countries whose law makes the bank government-controlled included), so the field is absent, the factor is 1 and the score (and the anchor0 the game seeds from it) is the original one bit for bit. AI countries never call the take or restore actions; a law that makes a bank independent again now also returns its credibility target gradually. Not done: scaling the penalty by how far policy departs from the bank's rule (the first half of finding M4). Minified names are those of build 26403824.
